Reproduction steps: 1. Launch Wazir Shell (`wa shell -c '? ...'`); 2. Execute `?` prompt or use `--model` / `/model` / `--permissions` / `/permissions`.
Expected & actual behavior: Expected: Honours pinned model, permission mode (`ask`/`auto`/`read-only`), loaded-model fallback on `MODEL_ADMISSION_DENIED`, prints provenance, `outcome.result`, and `outcome.errors` cleanly. Actual at baseline: `launchInteractiveWazirShell` passed `{}` to `executeTask`, dropped results/errors/provenance, and failed to honor `--model`/`--permissions` or offline diagnostic context.
Root cause: Inline `aiHandler` inside `launchInteractiveWazirShell` lacked `createShellAiHandler`, `attachShellPermissionPolicy`, `state.model`/`state.permissionMode` wiring, `engine.lifecycle.list()` fallback lookup, and result/provenance output formatting.

Reproduction steps: Classify ambiguous natural-language inputs `find broken tests`, `fix failing tests`, and `find relevant code for model routing` vs POSIX `find . -name '*.ts'`.
Expected & actual behavior: Expected: NL inputs route to `ai`; POSIX `find` flags/paths route to `shell`. Actual at baseline: `find broken tests` misrouted to `shell` (`/usr/bin/find`).
Root cause: `NATURAL_LANGUAGE_FOLLOWERS` lacked common NL nouns/adjectives (`broken`, `unused`, `missing`, `flaky`, `relevant`, `bugs`, `errors`, `issues`, `tests`, `models`, etc.) and lacked `looksLikeFindNaturalLanguage`.

Reproduction steps: Execute `! sleep 10` in Wazir Shell and send `AbortSignal` / `Ctrl+C`.
Expected & actual behavior: Expected: Terminates descendant `sleep` processes as well as outer shell cleanly leaving 0 orphans and restoring prompt (`exit 130`). Actual at baseline: only outer `child.kill('SIGINT')` was called, risking orphaned children and dangling abort listeners.
Root cause: `executeShellLine` and `rl.on('SIGINT')` signaled only the immediate `zsh`/`bash` child rather than traversing descendant PIDs (`pgrep -P`) with `terminateProcessTree` escalation.

Reproduction steps: Press TAB on builtins (`/permissions r`) and relative files/directories (`cd sample-`) in `state.cwd`.
Expected & actual behavior: Expected: Completes both builtins/directives and cwd-relative filesystem paths. Actual at baseline: inline static list did not complete filesystem paths or `/model`/`/permissions` directives.
Root cause: Inline `completer` in `launchInteractiveWazirShell` checked only a hardcoded command array with no `fs.readdirSync(state.cwd)` path completion or `/` directive prefix matching.

OS & shell: Expected: Builtins expand `$VAR` and `${VAR}` against `state.env` unless literal single-quoted. Actual at baseline: `cd` and `export` treated `$VAR` literally.
Files changed: Builtin `cd`, `export`, and bare `VAR=VAL` handlers called `unquoteShellArg` without expanding `$VAR` / `${VAR}` against `state.env`.

Reproduction steps: Run informational queries `? What operating system am I running?` or `? Find the relevant code for model routing`.
Expected & actual behavior: Expected: Treated as read-only inspection (`mutationRequired: false`) without failing verification for `0 files changed`. Actual on first live run (`exec-mwqvhbu9-1`): failed with `mutation required: task requires code modification but no files changed`.
Root cause: `TaskPlanner.analyze` `isCheckOrInspect` regex in `packages/core/src/services/planner.ts` omitted question/lookup words (`what`, `which`, `where`, `who`, `why`, `how`, `identify`, `find`, `locate`, `show`, `tell me`), causing `(!isCheckOrInspect)` to set `mutationRequired: true`.

Reproduction steps: Run `? What operating system am I running?` (`A01`) and `? Explain the architecture of this repository` (`A02`).
Expected & actual behavior: Expected: Agent has read/inspection tools (`glob`, `read`, `shell`) to inspect observed OS and repo files. Actual: `A01` hit `isConversationalFastPathRequest === true` (stripping tools) and `A02` routed to `wazir-chat` (`strategy: conversational-inference`, also stripping tools).
Root cause: `WORKSPACE_OR_TOOL_ACTION_RE` missed OS/hardware terms (`operating system`, `platform`, `uname`, `arch`), and `run.ts` left `targetAgentId` undefined when `mutationRequired === false`, while `createShellAiHandler` did not specify `agent: 'wazir-coding'`.

Reproduction steps: Launch `node apps/cli/dist/index.js shell --no-ai` in a PTY and run interactive child CLI `! node ask.cjs` reading from stdin.
Expected & actual behavior: Expected: Child receives `WAZIR_USER\\r` and exits, then parent Wazir Shell prompt returns cleanly. Actual: Parent `readline` raw-mode listener stayed open during `stdio: 'inherit'` child execution, consuming child keystrokes and wedging prompt return.
Root cause: Single long-lived `readline.createInterface` in `launchInteractiveWazirShell` kept `stdin` in raw mode while child owned FD 0. Fixed by closing `rl` and resetting `setRawMode(false)` before `executeShellLine`, forwarding `SIGINT` via `process.on('SIGINT')`, and recreating `rl` with updated history afterward.

Reproduction steps: Run coding/repair tasks (`A03`, `A04`) in non-TTY Wazir Shell `--permissions auto` where model invokes `npm test` or `cd <project> && node ... --test` via `shell`.
Expected & actual behavior: Expected: Safe workspace test commands inside `projectRoot` run cleanly under `auto` mode and dedicated `test` tools are preferred so non-TTY `shell-unknown-ask` denials do not poison passing verification. Actual: `PolicyEngine` escalated `npm test`/`node --test` in non-TTY to `deny`, poisoning `evaluation`.
Root cause: `buildQwenSystemPrompt` lacked explicit mandate preferring `test`/`build`/`lint`/`typecheck` tools over `shell`, and `attachShellPermissionPolicy` did not allow metacharacter-free `SAFE_AUTO_TEST_COMMAND_RE` test commands (with optional `cd` inside `projectRoot`) when `permissionMode === 'auto'`.

Reproduction steps: Run multi-turn `qwen3-coder:30b` coding/security tasks via Ollama (`A04`, `SEC02`).
Expected & actual behavior: Expected: Model XML fallback `<function=shell><parameter=command>...</parameter></function></tool_call>` without opening `<tool_call>` is parsed into a structured tool call. Actual: `turn.ts:143` and `xmlToolFallback.ts:169` early-returned when `<tool_call>` opening tag was absent, dropping tool calls (`toolCalls: []`).
Root cause: Ollama `qwen3-coder` template intermittently emits bare `<function=...></function></tool_call>` without `<tool_call>`. Updated `TOOL_CALL_BLOCK_RE`, `parseXmlToolCalls` guard, and `turn.ts:143` to invoke XML fallback whenever `content` contains `<tool_call>` or `<function=...>`.
